neighbours.label: The noun 'reason(s)' naming a cause in an explanatory assertion (one of the major reasons for, the chief reason for, several reasons why); synonyms (causes, factors, because of) are the near misses
fire: Poor drainage is one of the main reasons for the flooding in the valley.
The chief reason for the delay was a shortage of steel.
There are several reasons why the bridge was never finished.
High rents remain the biggest reason that young families leave the city.
Doctors list smoking among the leading reasons for the rise in lung disease.
Another reason for the crop failure was the late frost in May.
Cost is one of the major reasons that hospitals postpone upgrades.
The committee gave two reasons for rejecting the plan.
quiet: Poor drainage is one of the main causes of the flooding in the valley.
The delay happened because of a shortage of steel.
There are several factors behind the bridge never being finished.
High rents are the biggest problem that young families face in the city.
Doctors list smoking among the leading risks for lung disease.
The late frost in May also contributed to the crop failure.
Cost is one of the major obstacles that hospitals face with upgrades.
The committee gave two conditions for approving the plan.

predictions: 'one of the main reasons for', 'the chief reason for', 'several reasons why' reach 0.3-0.5 on reason(s). The same causal claims worded with causes, because of, factors, problem, risks, contributed to, obstacles stay under 0.1.
notes: Probe: 'one of the major reasons for poor concentration' 0.421 (' reasons'); 'effective home remedy' 0.093, 'some of the most sought-after courses' 0.065, 'What worries doctors is' 0.046, 'Dubai is the perfect destination' 0.029; narrative controls 0.000-0.034. Card: ' reasons' x3, ' reason' x3, ' due' x2, ' is' x3 in listicle prose ('one of the major reasons for failure', 'some of the top-notch courses', 'an effective home remedy', Arabic أسباب = reasons) (max 38, layer 24, broad 0.96%). Only the reasons configuration transferred from the card, so the label is the word; the - pole peaks on ' which', ' that', ' as'.
